findings: Definition of 'Business Day' differs between documents 01_msa.md (Section 1.2) and 04_sla.md (Section 2.1) The 'Business Day' definition in the Master Services Agreement (MSA) is different from the one defined in the Service Level and Support Schedule (SLAS). In the MSA, a Business Day means Monday to Friday, including public holidays. In the SLAS, a Business Day means Monday to Saturday, excluding US federal holidays. This difference could lead to confusion regarding when certain services are available.

Duplicate definition of 'Business Day' 01_msa.md (Section 1.2) and 04_sla.md (Section 2.1) Both the MSA and SLAS define a 'Business Day' as Monday to Saturday, including US federal holidays. This is redundant and could lead to confusion if both documents are used together.

Inconsistent definition of 'Deliverable' 01_msa.md (Section 1.4) and 02_sow.md (Section 6.2) The MSA defines a Deliverable as any item identified as such in a Statement of Work, while the Statement of Work specifically mentions Deliverables for each phase. This inconsistency could cause confusion if both documents are used together.

Conflicting definition of 'Security Incident' 02_sow.md (Section 7.1) and 03_dpa.md (Section 6.1) The Statement of Work defines a Security Incident as an unauthorised or unlawful access to, or acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data. The Data Processing Addendum, however, treats all Security Incidents as Priority 1 Incidents for the purposes of SLAS clause 5.1. This could cause ambiguity and may not be aligned with actual incident handling procedures.

The Exhibit A Acceptance document only mentions a 'Transition Period' in Section 4, which could cause confusion about its length.
